info.title: subkit engine
info.description: Backend workflow engine. See /docs for the interactive reference and /openapi.json for the raw spec. LLM clients can ground themselves on /llms.txt (index) or /llms-full.txt (full docs in one fetch), per https://llmstxt.org, and on /docs.json (every chapter in English and German as one JSON bundle).

bearerAuth.description: SubKit API key or an OAuth 2.1 access token issued by the MCP authorization server. A credential that carries a scope list is bounded by it: GET /metrics requires the metrics:read scope from API keys, RFC 8693 exchanged tokens and connection tokens alike, and the caller's role does not widen it.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow with PKCE. Browser login uses product-local API-key or direct OIDC adapters.

scopes.mcp:read: Read published content, resources, and product statistics
scopes.metrics:read: Read the operational counters exposed by GET /metrics — nothing else

task_runs.description: Task runs that started in the window, and how many of them are confirmed as completed or have failed by now.

groups.description: Group memberships, or null when the caller cannot read RBAC membership.

invite.description: Create the person as invited and issue their single-use invitation in the same step. Omitted: the person is active at once.

ask_before_writing.description: The person's rule: every step that writes asks first, even when the job or a saved rule covers it. Off unless chosen.

default_environment.description: The environment new workflows, tasks and approval dialogs start with.

timezone.description: The person's own time zone; null means the workspace time zone applies.

critical_breakthrough.description: Whether critical items notify at once despite the schedule. Off unless chosen.

save_new_notes.description: Whether new personal notes are learned from the person's own chat messages. On unless switched off. Personal notes are readable only by the person.

unset.description: Choices the person has not made yet; their values are the recommended ones.

invitation.description: Present once, right after this request prepared an invitation for the teammate. No mail was sent.

user_id.description: The teammate's person, once one exists.

invitation.description: member: the teammate is in the workspace. pending: an invitation is prepared and not yet accepted. needs_admin: an administrator has to invite this address first.

can_approve.description: Whether the teammate's role may grant what is asked of an approver: conversation:approve, task:grant and workflow:write. false means approval notifications stay with the asking person until an administrator changes the role. null while the teammate is not a person in the workspace yet.

missing_permissions.description: The approver permissions the teammate's role lacks; empty when can_approve.

pair.description: active: the workspace requires two people for every workflow approval. needs_second_approver: fewer than two people may approve; it starts once the partner has joined with a role that may approve. needs_admin: only an administrator switches the workspace to two-person approval.

from.description: Local time of day in the person's time zone, HH:MM.

to.description: Local time of day in the person's time zone, HH:MM.

days.description: Working days as ISO weekdays, 1 = Monday to 7 = Sunday. Monday to Friday when omitted. A window that crosses midnight belongs to the day it starts on.

at.description: Local time of day in the person's time zone, HH:MM.

SetupNotificationSchedule.description: When notifications reach the person. working_hours holds them outside the window and on other weekdays and delivers one summary at the next start; daily_digest delivers one summary at the chosen time. Times are read in the personal time zone and follow its clock changes. The schedule applies to push notifications and to the announcement hint on the Cockpit event stream; the attention list, the shared CLI inbox, chat channels and outbound webhooks are never delayed.

SetupSpend.description: The workspace's monthly AI spending limit in US dollars.

ask_before_writing.description: The person's rule: always ask before a step writes, even when the job covers it.

timezone.description: The person's time zone; null falls back to the workspace time zone.

critical_breakthrough.description: Opt in: a stopped production workflow and a stored secret that can no longer be read notify at once, also outside working hours and before the daily summary.

save_new_notes.description: Whether SubKit keeps learning personal notes from what the person writes in chats. Switching it off stops new notes; existing notes stay until the person forgets them.

monthly_spend_usd.description: How many US dollars SubKit may spend on AI per month in this workspace; 0 means no limit. Sets the workspace's monthly AI budget and needs identity:write.

oneOf.description: Two of us: one builds, one approves. Names the partner and asks for two-person workflow approval in the workspace.

paused.description: Whether push notifications and desktop banners are held back right now. Attention items and counts keep counting either way.

mode.description: until: the pause ends by itself at `until`. until_resumed: it lasts until resumed.

state.description: warning from 80 %. reached: chat, tasks and model steps in workflows pause. continued: an admin chose to go on without a limit this month.

choices.description: The limits setup offers; 0 means no limit.

online.description: True when the device sent a heartbeat within the last 45 s.

screenshot.description: True when the device's person can read the redacted screenshot of this step, kept for 30 days.

secrets.description: Vault handles the step uses, by name; never values.

repeated.description: True when the step runs once per item of a for_each, so the model is called once per item.

data_paths.description: The run data the step sends to the model, by placeholder path; never values.

model_calls.description: Each model step: the run sends step data to the workspace AI model and spends tokens.

tool_pins_compared.description: Present when the workflow calls MCP tools: whether each pinned tool description was compared with its server for this caller. It is only compared for a caller who may grant the approval.

target.description: Where the request goes: its method and the URL origin and path, without credentials or query values. url is null when the target is not a static http(s) address.

item.description: The folder id, website origin or app id that a device growth adds, the vault handle a new_secret growth adds, or the model step a new_model_call growth adds or widens.

model_call.description: Set when the change is a model step that sends step data to the AI model.

workflow_approvals.description: single: one person with workflow:write approves a workflow. pair: two different people both approve the same reviewed boundary before it takes effect.

eligible_approvers.description: Active people who hold workflow:write and may take one of the two slots.

ready.description: Whether pair approval can work: at least two eligible people exist.

state.description: pending: waits for a second person. approved: both approved and the execution authority exists. declined, withdrawn: closed by a person. expired: nobody approved within 72 hours or before the approval would have ended. stale: the workflow changed or the person who asked can no longer approve.

viewer_can_approve.description: Whether the caller may take the second slot right now; never true for the first approver.

MissingBindingEvidence.description: What a missing_binding step lacks: the kind of binding, the reference the step names and whether it was deleted or never existed in this workspace, a live connector with the same slug and driver when one exists, and the repair path.

invalid.description: True when the current version is stored in an earlier definition format. Everything below is read from the stored definition as written; a run is refused with `workflow_version_invalid` until the workflow is saved again.

visibility.description: Whether this caller may read the workflow's inbound hooks (`inbound_hook:read`) and schedules (`schedule:read`). When false the list is ABSENT, which is not the same as empty: the workflow may well have hooks or schedules this caller cannot see, so nothing about them — that there are none, or that all are approved — can be concluded.

hooks.description: The workflow's inbound hooks. Present — possibly empty — only when `visibility.hooks` is true.

tool_name.description: The name this workflow's own tool has WHEN the MCP catalog publishes it. Not every saved workflow is published to every client: the catalog depends on the caller's permissions and mode and lists a bounded number of workflow tools. `fallback` works either way.

schedules.description: The workflow's schedules. Present — possibly empty — only when `visibility.schedules` is true.

dev.description: `live_run_allowed`: an approval for the running version exists in this environment — unrevoked, inside its window, with runs left. It does NOT say the next run is admitted: admission also requires that the approval still matches the workflow's current effects and that those effects may run repeatedly, and holds or refuses the run otherwise. `held_preview_only`: no such approval; a call runs as a held preview that withholds writes.

prod.description: `live_run_allowed`: an approval for the running version exists in this environment — unrevoked, inside its window, with runs left. It does NOT say the next run is admitted: admission also requires that the approval still matches the workflow's current effects and that those effects may run repeatedly, and holds or refuses the run otherwise. `held_preview_only`: no such approval; a call runs as a held preview that withholds writes.

rules.description: Configured roles and unexpired grants for this workflow, visible only with rbac:read. These rules do not establish an authenticated caller or bypass credential restrictions, account state, or effect admission.

start_access.description: Current caller's workflow:run permission evaluated with credential ceilings; not an effect approval or a guarantee that a run is admitted. External authenticated callers need this permission too. Inbound hooks have their separately configured verifiers and are listed under hooks.

post.description: Form-encoded OAuth 2.1 token endpoint. `grant_type=authorization_code` and `grant_type=refresh_token` serve MCP clients. `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` (RFC 8693) turns an API key into a short-lived Bearer token: send `subject_token=<api key>` and `subject_token_type=urn:subkit:params:oauth:token-type:api-key`; no client_id or client secret. The response carries `access_token`, `token_type=Bearer`, `issued_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token`, `expires_in` and `scope`, and no refresh token. The token is accepted everywhere the key is (same principal, tenant, roles and allow-lists; audit rows carry `via: token_exchange`). Revoking, expiring or rotating the key refuses its tokens at once. Tool calls and elicitations are NOT copied — re-running them would duplicate side effects. Caveat: assistant message content that references `tool_call_id` values from the source will retain those refs even though the corresponding tool_call rows are not in the fork; the CLI renderer treats unknown ids as plain text, but audit-log readers should be aware. Each copied message gets a fresh `created_at` (set to fork-time) so the fork's timeline orders cleanly; the source's original timestamps are preserved in the source conversation, joinable via `forked_from` in the audit metadata. The fork is hard-capped at the most recent 5,000 messages up to and including the anchor; when the cap fires the response sets `truncated: true` and the audit row records the original source count.
